headline: Diplomatic Gift-Exchange Specialist Forced Into Early Retirement After Realizing He Accidentally Gifted Switzerland A Single Block of Amul Processed Cheddar
body:
The Ministry of External Affairs’ lead protocol officer, Rajesh Varma, submitted his resignation this morning after the realization that the ‘premium artisanal collection’ presented to the Swiss delegation consisted entirely of mass-produced, individually wrapped orange squares. Varma, who spent three weeks curating the gift, reportedly mistook a neighborhood convenience store’s ‘Buy-One-Get-One’ clearance bin for a hidden cache of rare Himalayan yak-milk delicacies.

“I honestly thought the packaging was just a minimalist, avant-garde choice by a struggling mountain cheesemaker,” Varma told reporters while packing his desk. “When the Swiss President opened the first box and saw the familiar plastic film, I assumed it was a local custom to protect the cheese from the Delhi humidity. It wasn’t until he started trying to make a toasted sandwich in the middle of the bilateral talks that I realized we hadn't quite hit the level of luxury expected at the G20 level.”

Witnesses at the meeting confirmed that the Swiss delegation displayed professional stoicism, with one diplomat even remarking that the ‘processed texture’ possessed a certain ‘industrial nostalgic quality’ missing from the Swiss Alps. Varma, however, could not be consoled, despite being offered a transfer to the stationary department to oversee the procurement of pens with non-leaking ink.

“I’ve already begun an internal investigation into my own eyesight,” Varma added. “I spent six months looking for a rare, cave-aged gouda, and ended up giving a world leader a product that is currently being used to garnish a roadside vada pav stall. My career in soft diplomacy is officially toast.”
